sceneFormat.title: Scene format — the Fountain dialect
sceneFormat.intro: Scenes are plain text. The block editor reads and writes this dialect, so what you type in Source round-trips with the Write view.

settings.title: Settings — global toggles
settings.intro: Per-user preferences (the gear in the status bar). The first two change only what the **Write** view shows — your prose and the Source view always keep the tags.

rows.v: Delivery (mood) parentheticals in Write — for visual-novel-style writing
[start → end] timecodes in Write — for subtitle / transcript work
Advanced: makes Source editable, saved to the file verbatim — lets you change form-locked frontmatter (like a page’s id). Off by default; a bad edit is written as-is.

worldPages.title: World pages
items: Add a page from the World sidebar — hover a group and click +.
**Properties** edits the page's fields and its **phase** (draft → developing → canon → archived).
**Phase** is editorial maturity; **status** is in-world state (active, deceased…).
Preview renders the wiki panel; Source is the raw Markdown an agent reads.

rows.v: Ask about the open work — it reads scenes/world pages and can queue page edits for you
Background page edits (from Chat or /agent) — run while you keep writing; review & apply each
Describe a change to the open page — it’s queued as a Task, not applied inline
Saved, reusable instructions (Reformat, Placeholders, your own) — the picker in /agent

pageEdits.title: Page edits — append vs replace
pageEdits.intro: Every saved prompt (and queued edit) is one of two kinds. Applying a finished edit is a single step, so one **Cmd/Ctrl+Z** undoes it.

rows.v: The AI returns only new text, added to the end of the page — for drafting / scaffolding
The AI returns the whole page rewritten — for reformatting / revising existing text

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
shortcuts.pageTab: Switch the view tab — Write · Preview · Source (custody: Chart · Records · Write · Preview · Source)
shortcuts.undo: Undo the last applied edit — add Shift to redo
shortcuts.compose: Composition mode — hide all chrome (Esc exits)
shortcuts.split: Split the block at the caret (new block below)
